name: go-grpc-middleware-9150cbd1-blind30-ots
instr:
# Diagnosing go-grpc-middleware without a test suite

Almost nothing can be exercised end to end at the moment. Standing up a local endpoint that presents its own self-signed identity material aborts partway through producing that throwaway material, announcing a failure even though the material itself came out fine, so every scenario that needs a live connection dies during setup. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. Once that blocker is cleared the rest of the damage becomes visible.

The bundled example responder answers with wrong numbers. A plain single call comes back with a fixed counter of 43 where 42 has always been the answer. The one-way flow of replies numbers its messages from one rather than zero, and the two-way echo does the same, as a second and independent slip: each reply carries a sequence number one higher than the position it was sent at, although the echoed text itself is intact. Sending up a sequence of messages and waiting for the single summary reply no longer works at all — the receiving side stops as soon as the first message lands and finishes without ever sending the summary back.

Watching what happens to a call is unreliable from the moment it opens until the moment its record is written out. Opening any streaming call from the calling side goes wrong as the stream is created: the call is booked as already complete the instant it starts, and no usable stream is handed back.
